The power spec is the only failing metric. Total supply current is about 1.715 mW / 1.8 V ≈ 0.95 mA, while the 1.4 mW limit allows about 0.78 mA. In this topology, M1 is a source follower with M2 as its NMOS current sink, and M2 mirrors the reference M3. The mirror ratio is (39.57/0.984)/(0.42/0.984) ≈ 94, so M3's width of 0.42 µm is the most likely corruption. A too-small reference device inflates the mirror ratio and pushes the bias current above target. The other metrics (gain, f3dB, GBW, swing, output DC) have margin, so the signal path looks intact.

```json
{"ranking": ["M3", "M2", "M1"], "fault": "Reference mirror device M3 width corrupted to 0.42 um (too small), inflating the M2/M3 mirror ratio (~94x) and over-biasing the M2 current sink, which raises total power to ~1.7 mW; width should be scaled up to bring the bias current down to ~0.78 mA."}
```
